newsitem.title: SPAIN: Gonzalez says Spain court pressured on "dirty war".
newsitem.headline: Gonzalez says Spain court pressured on "dirty war".

text.p: Former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez said on Tuesday Supreme Court judges had been "pressured" into ordering the declassification of secret spy papers that allegedly implicate him in a 1980s "dirty war".

Gonzalez, whose Socialist party is accused of masterminding hit squads against ETA Basque separatist rebels while in power, told a news conference the court's decision last month highlighted flaws in the justice system.
"There are plenty of people, absolutely irresponsible, who for months have been pressuring the (Supreme Court) in a shameless and public way," he said.

The Supreme Court ordered the government to open 13 of 17 secret files which lower courts said could provide evidence that Gonzalez and his associates set up and ran the "dirty war", which killed 28 people from 1983 to 1987.
One third of those assassinated were not affiliated with ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), which has killed some 800 people in its struggle for independence.

Gonzalez did not name names but ex-officials from his administration on trial for the "dirty war" have said the appearance of the documents and the subsequent investigations was a conspiracy of aggrieved rivals, judges and journalists.

Spain's two major newspapers have published copies of the files and editorials called for declassification as an important step toward finally clearing up what has been seen as an ugly mark against Spain's young democracy.
